label: Power Rabi
axes: Readout signal versus drive pulse amplitude at fixed pulse shape. Three layouts ship under one figure name. (a) The common one: a grid of small panels, one per qubit, each a 1-D trace — horizontal axis is drive pulse amplitude, with a twin top axis giving the dimensionless prefactor relative to the currently stored amplitude; vertical axis is the readout observable, either an analog IQ magnitude or a discriminated qubit-state count (both occur across runs and the family does not fix which). A jagged raw trace and a smooth fitted curve are overplotted in two colours. (b) The error-amplification variant: per-qubit 2-D maps over a narrow amplitude window — horizontal axis drive amplitude (same prefactor twin axis), vertical axis number of repeated pulses, colour the readout observable, plus a vertical marker line at the chosen amplitude. (c) A rarer 2-D map of drive amplitude against readout frequency detuning, colour the readout observable, with no per-qubit panelling.
correct_signature: In the 1-D sweep layout only (bullets 1-6 apply to it alone; the 2-D pulse-count map is judged solely by the fringe bullet below and never by looking for a single sine): one smooth sinusoidal excursion dominates the trace: a single broad extremum with the curve falling away on both sides at comparable rates. Whether it is a crest or a trough is set by readout sign — both are equally valid and neither is evidence of a problem.

The peak-to-trough swing of the smooth component is several times the point-to-point scatter, so the arch is legible with the fitted curve mentally erased; you could sketch the trend from the raw trace alone.

The fitted overlay sits inside the noise band along the whole sweep, with scatter falling on both sides of it everywhere — no stretch where a run of consecutive points all lie above the curve and another stretch where they all lie below.
The curvature turns over inside the swept range: the extremum has data descending away from it on both sides, rather than a ramp still climbing or still falling as it reaches an edge.

If more than one period is visible, successive extrema keep constant spacing and comparable height. Several periods across the window is a legitimate signature (it means a large pending correction), not a defect — the rhythm staying regular is what matters, and contrast may taper without that being wrong.
The low-amplitude end approaches a flat baseline and departs from it smoothly, with no step discontinuity or sudden level change partway through the sweep.

In the pulse-count map variant: one family of curved fringes converges on a single amplitude. At that amplitude one fringe runs vertical - at the same amplitude from the lowest pulse-count row to the highest - while the fringes on either side bend toward it and crowd together as pulse count grows; the marker line sits at that convergence with fan visible on either side of it.

failure_appearance.wrong_peak: In the pulse-count map (inferred from the geometry of accepted runs, not witnessed on a rejected run): the marker line sits at an amplitude where the fringes are still slanted and crowding, while the one fringe that stays vertical across the whole pulse-count range lies more than a fringe spacing away.
failure_appearance.no_signal: The trace is a uniform band of scatter with no smooth component at all, and the fitted overlay collapses to a nearly flat line or a bow so shallow no eye would have drawn it through those points. The vertical spread of the raw trace looks identical at every amplitude, with no region where the excursion exceeds the local jitter. In the pulse-count map variant the panel is a field of unrelated blocks with no curved fringe family and no amplitude where anything converges.
failure_appearance.noisy: A smooth component is present but its crest-to-trough swing is comparable to the point-to-point scatter, so the arch is only readable because the fitted curve is drawn on it. Single samples routinely excurse past the fitted extremum, and adjacent points jump by a sizeable fraction of the entire swing. In the pulse-count map variant the fringes are recognisable only in patches and break up over part of the pulse-count range, so the convergence amplitude cannot be pinned by eye.
failure_appearance.feature_present_fit_failed: Real curvature is present but the overlay parts company with it: the data climb and then flatten toward one end while the fitted curve turns over and pulls away, leaving a run of consecutive points all on one side of the line near that edge. The extremum the fit implies then sits at or beyond the edge of the swept range, with no data turning back on the far side to support it.

abstain_when: The figure is the amplitude-versus-detuning map variant: all visible variation runs along the detuning axis and the amplitude axis carries no fringe structure, so there is nothing on the claimed axis to confirm or refute.

A multi-panel grid is shown but the claim does not identify which panel it belongs to — panels within one image routinely span textbook arches through to pure scatter, so picking one to judge would be a guess.
The extremum, or the fringe convergence, sits hard against the edge of the swept range: the picture cannot show whether the true optimum lies just outside the window.
The fitted overlay is absent, or the raw trace and the overlay are on visibly different vertical scales, so their agreement cannot be assessed from the picture.
Axis labels or the colour scale are unreadable at the delivered resolution, or the trace is clipped flat over part of the sweep so the true swing is hidden.
notes:
Evidence is thin and one-sided: five archived figures from a single multi-qubit archive, all from runs the node ACCEPTED. No node-rejected run exists in the archive for this family, so `wrong_peak` and `drifted` are left null rather than invented — neither was observed unambiguously, and a maintainer adding them later should ground them on a real rejected run.

Most important caveat for the judge: acceptance is recorded per RUN, but panels inside a single accepted run range from textbook single arches to flat scatter with a nearly-flat fit line. A run-level accept is therefore NOT evidence that any given panel is good. Judge per panel, and never let "this run was accepted" propagate to a panel that shows nothing. The `no_signal`, `noisy` and `feature_present_fit_failed` appearances above were all read off panels sitting inside accepted runs.

Two readout flavours occur on the vertical axis (analog IQ magnitude, and discriminated qubit-state counts) and the extremum sign flips freely between panels of the same run — a trough is as correct as a crest. Do not treat either as a defect.

Period count is not a quality criterion. A window spanning several periods simply means the stored amplitude is far off and a large correction is pending; the figure is still a valid signature. Rejecting on "too many oscillations" would throw away good data. Equally, do not require the extremum to land at any particular prefactor value — where it lands is the measurement's answer, not a precondition.

Localizer is 1d for both the 1-D sweep and the pulse-count map: in both, the quantity being claimed is a single amplitude and it can be pointed at (a curve extremum, or the vertical convergence of the fringe fan). The amplitude-versus-detuning map variant is the exception — it localizes nothing on the amplitude axis and belongs in abstain, not in a verdict.

Marker lines in the pulse-count variant were repeatedly seen pinned to the extreme edge of the narrow amplitude window with the fan convergence at or past that edge. That is a bracketing problem, not a peak-selection error, and it is why "extremum at the window edge" is an abstain trigger rather than a rejection.
